characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy controls the demonstrator development work, determining whether the project produces credible evidence that platform-neutral authentication is architecturally possible. It maps MitID's platform dependencies, prototypes FIDO2/WebAuthn and fallback mechanisms on GrapheneOS or comparable privacy-respecting environments, and generates non-production technical artifacts. Success is measured by delivering two working demonstrators that prove secure, standards-based access without exclusive reliance on Apple or Google as trust anchors, thereby validating the claim that resilient alternatives exist.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever directly enables Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy by providing the concrete technical evidence necessary to justify platform-neutrality requirements. When demonstrators prove feasibility, the resulting credibility makes policy arguments and procurement language substantially harder for incumbents to dismiss as speculative. Coalition Building Strategy also benefits, as tangible technical work attracts academic researchers and security experts who strengthen advocacy credibility.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Technical Feasibility Strategy creates tension with EU Standards Engagement Strategy over resource allocation and timeline. Deep engagement with European standards bodies requires sustained policy-facing activity that competes with developer time and budget. Additionally, choosing highly secure but narrow FIDO2-only demonstrators may limit the Coalition Building Strategy's ability to attract technology-diverse partners, whereas exploring blockchains and DIDs risks extending scope and undermining Procurement Influence Strategy's credibility with conservative Danish authorities.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy reframes digital identity dependency as a public-sector resilience and continuity-of-service problem rather than purely a privacy issue. It submits formal proposals to Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, influences regulatory language, and shapes the terms under which AltID procurement decisions are evaluated. Success metrics include securing formal written responses from authorities, achieving inclusion of platform-neutrality language in official design documents, and shifting institutional risk perception toward supplier concentration as a contingency-planning concern.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy amplifies Coalition Building Strategy by creating legitimacy and media attention that recruits additional stakeholders. It also reinforces Technical Feasibility Strategy: credible policy framing makes demonstrators more persuasive by anchoring them to formal institutional concerns. Procurement Influence Strategy depends critically on Policy Advocacy laying groundwork; without prior policy legitimation, procurement-focused language appears disconnected from institutional priorities.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy conflicts with EU Standards Engagement Strategy over message consistency and institutional focus. Emphasizing national resilience and continuity may alienate EU-facing partners who prioritize harmonized European standards. Additionally, broadening advocacy to include privacy and democratic accountability (versus narrower continuity framing) risks diluting the message and attracting coalition members whose priorities create friction in Procurement Influence Strategy negotiations with conservative Danish authorities.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy expands the constituency supporting platform-neutral digital identity from narrow technical experts to civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, academic researchers, contingency planners, and sympathetic legislators. It manages stakeholder engagement, identifies and recruits lead voices, navigates conflicting priorities, and consolidates disparate concerns into coherent advocacy positions. Success is measured by coalition size, diversity, public visibility, and demonstrable pressure on procurement and standards-setting institutions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Coalition Building Strategy directly enables Policy Advocacy Strategy by providing a broader, more visible constituency that makes policy arguments statistically harder to ignore. It also strengthens Procurement Influence Strategy by mobilizing diverse stakeholders who can credibly testify to supplier concentration risk across multiple domains. Technical Feasibility Strategy benefits from coalition support; academic researchers and security experts from the coalition can participate in or review demonstrator work, enhancing technical credibility.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Coalition Building Strategy creates internal friction with Policy Advocacy Strategy when coalition members prioritize privacy and democratic accountability over continuity-of-service framing, forcing advocacy messaging to accommodate competing priorities and potentially weakening focus. Recruiting internal dissidents from MitID operators and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen may also alienate institutional partners whose cooperation Procurement Influence Strategy depends on, creating a trade-off between external pressure and insider engagement.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy shapes requirements language in AltID and related digital identity procurement documents, ensuring platform-neutrality, fallback access, and supplier-diversity considerations are explicitly encoded in vendor evaluation criteria and contracting terms. It translates technical feasibility and policy advocacy into binding procurement specifications. Success metrics include documented inclusion of platform-neutral or fallback-authentication language in official procurement documents, measurable impact on vendor selection, and sustained reduction in exclusive platform dependency.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Procurement Influence Strategy depends entirely on Policy Advocacy Strategy and Technical Feasibility Strategy for credibility. Policy advocacy establishes institutional receptiveness; technical demonstrators prove feasibility; together they create the evidence base for procurement language. Coalition Building Strategy strengthens Procurement Influence by mobilizing stakeholders who can pressure procurement officials and testify to the business case for supplier diversity and resilience.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Procurement Influence Strategy conflicts with EU Standards Engagement Strategy over jurisdictional scope and authority. National procurement intervention may be perceived as inconsistent with EU harmonization goals if EU standards simultaneously permit exclusive platform dependency. Additionally, specific procurement language favoring platform-neutral vendors may trigger vendor gaming, regulatory capture, or legal challenges that undermine implementation, whereas vague language satisfies Technical Feasibility Strategy concerns about avoiding overcommitment but weakens actual procurement impact.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy channels project findings into relevant European Digital Identity Wallet, eIDAS2, and related technical working groups, aligning Danish advocacy with broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, and reduced platform lock-in. It positions the project as a contributor to EU-level standardization discussions rather than a purely national initiative. Success metrics include documented input to EU bodies, measurable alignment of project recommendations with published EU standards materials, and stretch-goal contribution to language supporting platform-neutral access mechanisms in European Identity Wallet frameworks.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy amplifies the reach of Technical Feasibility Strategy and Policy Advocacy Strategy by embedding Danish insights into European standards, increasing the pressure on all member states and platforms to accommodate platform-neutral requirements. It also strengthens Coalition Building Strategy by connecting Danish stakeholders to European networks of researchers, regulators, and civil-society organizations, creating a broader constituency for platform neutrality across the EU.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy creates resource and focus conflicts with Procurement Influence Strategy by diverting attention toward European bodies whose decision timelines may not align with Danish AltID procurement windows. Additionally, EU standards discussions are heavily influenced by large platform vendors and incumbent identity operators, which may pressure the project to soften or generalize platform-neutrality language, thereby weakening both the standards outcome and the credibility signal that Technical Feasibility Strategy and Policy Advocacy Strategy depend on for national procurement impact.
